svg.aria-label: Figure 2.3: The Giza Food and Supply Machine — Logistics and Division of Labor
svg.text: How Egypt's coinless ration state linked Delta herds, river stone barges, Sinai copper, a planned town, and organized teams

g.text: Young male cattle (1–2 yrs), sheep & goats
Locals ate pigs & older stock; prime meat went south
Tura (6–9 mi SE) to Akhet-Khufu · under Ankhhaf
Sinai ore via Wadi al-Jarf (74 mi S of Suez)
Merer's same royal crews stored Nile logs in caves
Soft copper chisels blunted fast on limestone
On-site furnaces recast tools (no local tin or iron)
17-ft (5.2 m) paved streets · guarded gates (c. 2558–2472 BCE)
Standardized emmer loaves, beer, beef, mutton & Nile fish
Honored tombs & healed fractures — paid labor tax, not slaves
Far below Herodotus's 100,000 rumor · every team had one job

text.tspan: Pulling young workers, cattle, grain, copper, and stone from every district into Giza's coinless ration

svg.text: network knitted scattered Nile towns into one working kingdom. (Workers' town remains at Heit el-Ghurab mostly date to c. 2558–2472 BCE.)
